sections.heading: Headway vs Alma: Overview
sections.content: Headway and Alma are both designed to help therapists accept insurance without the traditional headaches of credentialing and claims management. Headway positions itself as a streamlined credentialing and billing partner, while Alma offers a more comprehensive platform that includes community features, scheduling, and practice tools alongside insurance support.

sections.heading: Fee Structure
sections.content: Both platforms take a percentage of insurance reimbursements rather than charging large upfront fees. Alma has tiered membership options with different fee percentages. The exact percentages vary and should be confirmed directly with each platform as they negotiate different rates with different payers.

sections.heading: Platform Differences
sections.content: Alma provides more of an all-in-one platform experience with built-in scheduling, notes, telehealth, and a strong clinician community for networking and referrals. Headway is more focused on the core insurance workflow - credentialing, claims, and getting therapists paid. If you already have an EHR you love, Headway integrates. If you want everything in one place, Alma provides more tools.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: Choose based on your practice setup:

recommendations.when: You already have an EHR and telehealth platform you like, and just want help with insurance credentialing and billing
You want an all-in-one platform with community, want a stronger referral network, or are building your practice from scratch
Some providers use both to maximize payer coverage, though this requires managing two platforms

faqs.q: Can I use both Headway and Alma?
faqs.a: Yes, some providers use both to maximize their insurance panel coverage. However, you'll need to manage two platforms and their respective fees.

Both have extensive payer networks including major carriers like Aetna, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare, and various Blue Cross Blue Shield plans. Coverage varies by state and may change, so check with each platform for your specific location.

faqs.q: Do I need a separate EHR with Headway?
faqs.a: Yes, Headway focuses on credentialing and billing. You'll need your own EHR for documentation. Headway integrates with several popular EHRs.
